title: Honest chart or trick?
instruction: What is fine, and what does a chart that wants to fool you have?

items.text: The Y axis starts at zero
items.why: The heights of the bars match the real values.
Then a small difference looks huge.
You know what the chart measures and in what.

items.text: The chart starts in just the year when things look good
items.why: A picked period hides what it was like before.

items.text: A bar chart to compare classes
items.why: Bars side by side are easy to compare.
A figure twice as tall is also twice as wide, so it looks like four times as much.

items.text: A line chart for the temperature during a week
items.why: A line shows how a value changes over time.

items.text: A pie with 15 slices and no labels
items.why: So many slices without labels can't be compared. You don't know which is which.

debrief: An honest chart has labelled axes, a sensible scale and a suitable type. Tricks change the impression, not the data: a cut-off axis, a picked period, pictures instead of bars.
